editorial:
Imagine being a young guy who believes the world is perfect and everyone is honest. That is exactly where you start with this story. You follow a naive man who heads into the real world with big dreams and a heart full of love, only to find out that people can be cruel and selfish. It feels like a slow burn that focuses on the gap between what we want life to be and how it actually works. The vibe is very serious and emotional, making you feel the weight of every mistake the main character makes as he tries to navigate a society that does not share his kindness.

What really makes this work is the acting, as you can see the pain on the lead's face as his bubble bursts. The pace is a bit slow, which might bore some of you, but it helps you feel the sadness of the story. If you enjoy deep dramas about life lessons, you should definitely give this a try. You can find it by renting it on Apple TV for a quick watch, or if you really love high quality, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is the way to go for the best picture.
endingExplained: Everything falls apart when the main character realizes his idealism cannot save him or the people he loves. He learns that being a good person is not always enough to win in a harsh world. The movie wraps up with him facing a sad reality where his dreams are crushed. He ends up broken and alone, showing you that ignoring the truth about human nature usually leads to a painful wake-up call.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves stories about life lessons and old-school dramas.
